clue.text: Seventh note put out by one seeking restoration for actor

indicators.note: the note is ejected from the word for the restorer, so its letters are removed

parts.note: a Jacobite sought to restore the Stuart kings to the British throne
te (or ti) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note is being expelled by a royalist rebel, apparently for the benefit of a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out by' drops the note. 'restoration' suggests building work, but Jacobites wanted the exiled Stuart kings restored after 1688.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Derek Jacobi is a celebrated English stage and screen performer.

clue.text: Large sum of money put in court reportedly for a crock?

parts.note: pots of money means a great deal of it

indicators.note: says the word for being tried in court is only spoken, so a same-sounding spelling is used

parts.note: a case that is heard is tried before a court

explanation.surface: A fortune is apparently being argued in court over something worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns HEARD into HERD. The question mark flags that crock here is a broken bit of earthenware, not a fool or old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A crock can mean a broken fragment of earthenware, which is exactly a shard of pottery.

clue.text: Smear largely dividing local family trying to maintain an image?

indicators.note: the cut-down smear goes between the pub and the family, splitting them

parts.note: a local is a British term for one's nearby pub
one's relations are one's family

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to lick paint on is to smear it thinly

explanation.surface: A slander spreads through the village pub and a family fights to keep its good name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' leaves LIC, which 'dividing' splits the pub and family words with. A British 'local' is one's neighbourhood pub; a lick of paint is a thin smear.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity work is the business of managing and protecting how an organisation is seen.

clue.text: Beginning to inspect zip, no ordinary fashionable phenomenon

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken
says the letter for ordinary is absent from the word for zip

parts.note: zip is slang for zero or nil

explanation.surface: An inspector checks a zip and finds it is nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops the O for ordinary. 'zip' reads as a fastener but is slang for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Something currently in vogue is a trendy craze everyone wants a part of.

clue.text: Former minister inherits a messy set of unrealistic plans

parts.note: Barbara Castle was a Labour cabinet minister in the 1960s and 70s

indicators.note: untidy, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An ex-minister comes into a disordered set of possessions in a legacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' rearranges INHERITS A to SINTHEAIR. Barbara Castle was a well-known British Labour minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes daydream schemes with no foundation in reality.

clue.text: Check filthy place on road close to cafe

parts.note: a pigsty is the byword for a dirty place
the M1 is a British motorway, its 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: the end letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: An inspector checks a grubby roadside cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main British motorway north from London; written MI it gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to block or thwart it, a synonym.

clue.text: It's said to be vital with small fruit

indicators.note: points to a spoken version of the following words

parts.note: vital gives key and small gives wee (Scottish for little), together pronounced as one word

explanation.surface: A small piece of fruit is claimed to be essential to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said to be' asks for KEY plus WEE spoken aloud. Wee is Scottish and northern English for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese gooseberry is a fuzzy green-fleshed fruit, sold under this name.

clue.text: Lofty aura found in church a lot

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, across the word gap

explanation.surface: An elevated atmosphere is often encountered in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' hides the answer in churCH A LOt.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint's glowing ring hovers above the head, an elevated radiance.

clue.text: For audience, make facility for tea?

indicators.note: for listeners, so a spoken match is wanted

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put the kettle on for a gathered crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For audience' asks for a word sounding like EARN. 'make' tempts as brew, but means earn.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal vessel with a tap boils water to serve tea at gatherings.

clue.text: Get a sign of decay with end coming to the fore

indicators.text: with end coming to the fore
indicators.note: the word's final letter moves round to its front

parts.note: a taint is a trace of rot or corruption

explanation.surface: Someone receives a mark of rot that has moved to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with end coming to the fore' moves the last T forward, making TTAIN. 'Get' looks like 'receive' but means achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something you have aimed for is to achieve or reach it.

clue.text: East German once staying in Florida, a wrinkly?

indicators.note: the German sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
Ossi was the nickname for a citizen of the former East Germany

explanation.surface: A former East German retiree lives out their days in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossi was slang for an East German before reunification. Florida is a famous retirement destination, which shapes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slangy, mildly mocking terms for an elderly, old-fashioned person.

clue.text: Boater perhaps halting around island to return hostile communication

parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat

indicators.note: means the built-up piece is read backwards
the limping word goes around the island letter

parts.note: halting walk is a lame one

explanation.surface: A man in a straw hat limps round an island and back, angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts LAME round I to make LIAME, which 'to return' turns into EMAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive letters or messages sent to a target are poisonous correspondence.

clue.text: With day gone, need conceived for revised corporate discussion?

indicators.note: says a letter departs from the jumbled words
reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a day off, a need is thought up for a reworked business conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' drops a D from NEED CONCEIVED FOR, and 'revised' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A business meeting held over cameras and screens is a remote corporate exchange.

clue.text: Ignore shot on square?

definitions.meaning: to snub someone is to ignore them pointedly
in cricket, a stroke played square of the wicket on the off side

explanation.surface: Someone disregards a strike made on a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a square shot goes at right angles to the pitch; this one is a classic off-side stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Snubbing someone and a cricket stroke square on the off side share one short word.

clue.text: Fly trapped in tin for a bit

indicators.note: the insect sits inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a midge is a tiny fly

explanation.surface: A fly is stuck in a can for a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped in' places the insect inside tin's chemical symbol; 'Fly' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, a scrap or trace, is an informal word for a little.

clue.text: Old woman harbouring love for departed flier

indicators.note: sheltering inside, so the score of zero goes within

parts.note: one's old woman is slang for mother, MA
love means nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A mother cherishes a loved one who has flown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' puts O inside MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct giant flightless bird of New Zealand is long gone; flier is ironic here.

clue.text: Abuse? It's quickly detected in bistro perhaps when consuming drink (calorie-free)

indicators.note: the French word swallows the drink

parts.note: vite is French for quickly, a word heard in a French bistro

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so that letter goes

parts.note: cola is a fizzy drink
C is an abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: Wolfing a diet drink in a bistro is apparently a kind of abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' leaves OLA, which 'when consuming' places in the French word. A bistro is a small French restaurant, hence a French word for quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat something with disrespect, or break a rule, is to abuse it.

clue.text: Girl embracing fashion without a modicum of elegance or generosity

indicators.note: the girl's word goes round the cut-down fashion word

parts.note: lass is a northern English and Scottish word for a girl

indicators.note: means the letter A is taken out

parts.note: something all the rage is in fashion

indicators.note: only a scrap, the first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A girl takes up an unfussy style and shows a touch of grace or kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves RGE, which 'embracing' puts in the girl; 'a modicum of' adds E. Fashion is 'all the rage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish giving of money or gifts is a liberal open-handedness.

clue.text: Evidence, say, of bitter work unit blocking renovation of Tube

indicators.note: the unit of work sits inside the rearranged letters, blocking them
a renovation remakes something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the erg is a physics unit of work

explanation.surface: Something about bitter work on an Underground line held up by renovations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovation of' makes BEUT; 'blocking' sets the work unit inside. Bitter is a British style of beer, and the Tube is London's Underground, both misleading here.
explanation.definitionFit: A big belly from drinking is visible proof of a fondness for ale.

clue.text: One sitting in normal section of joint not good with an air that's suspect

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level

indicators.note: means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: a ligament is part of a joint, binding bones

indicators.note: something dubious, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone with a dodgy bad joint sits about with a suspicious air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes G from LIGAMENT, leaving LIAMENT; 'that's suspect' rearranges AN AIR into ARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the House is one who sits there; sitting is the formal term for attendance.

clue.text: Culinary eccentric turning out starters of inedible roast — madness!

indicators.note: odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged
evicting, so those letters are removed from the pool
takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: An odd cook throws out an inedible roast in a fit of rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' removes I and R from CULINARY; 'eccentric' rearranges the remaining CULNAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Insanity or wild folly is the meaning; it's a direct synonym.

clue.text: Blanket from a fine country lacking finish

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil leads

indicators.note: the country loses its last letter

parts.note: Ghana is a West African country

explanation.surface: A rug is shipped from a pleasant country that has no end to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking finish' trims GHANA to GHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted or crocheted woollen throw, as named after the country, is this kind of blanket.

clue.text: Group of parties that is beginning to rally for march

parts.note: a front is an alliance of political parties
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: An alliance gets ready to rally for a protest walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'march' looks like a protest walk, but it is a border region.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is an old word for a borderland, such as the Welsh Marches.

clue.text: Grub a factor in foundation

definitions.meaning: to grub is to dig or rummage, as a pig does in soil
the base or underlying cause that something grows from

explanation.surface: Food turns out to be a key element in a firm base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food but is the verb for digging about.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummaging in earth and the underlying base of a plant or idea share the same word.

clue.text: Come out from English lake having swallowed bit of gunge

indicators.note: the lake word takes in the letter

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

indicators.note: just the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Something rises from an English lake that has taken in some slime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having swallowed' puts G inside MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear or come into view is to come out from somewhere.

clue.text: Bird that stings almost visible in sun

indicators.note: seen inside the suntan word

parts.note: a tan is what the sun gives you

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: ouch is what you cry when something stings

explanation.surface: A bird with a sting is nearly visible in the sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves OUC, which 'visible in' places within the sun's gift. 'that stings' seems to describe the bird but is the cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical American bird with an enormous colourful beak.

clue.text: Weapon that's leaking, we hear

indicators.note: says the word is matched by its spoken form

parts.note: something oozy is seeping or leaking

explanation.surface: A gun is said to be dribbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns OOZY into UZI.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact Israeli submachine gun, named after its designer Uziel Gal.

clue.text: In hospital, get cold in medical examination

indicators.note: the cold letter goes inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A patient catches a chill in hospital during a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN is short for sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaging procedure such as an MRI is a common diagnostic test.
